clue.text: Cheese and fruit mostly served with minced beef

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit
a burger is a patty of minced beef

explanation.surface: A cheese course with fruit and a beefburger on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Limburger is a strong-smelling soft cheese from the Limburg region of Belgium and the Netherlands.

clue.text: Permission to depart

definitions.meaning: ... is permission, as in ... of absence

explanation.surface: Asking to be allowed to go.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun leave is formal permission; the verb leave means to go away, so one word covers both senses.

clue.text: Standard of dinner mostly OK

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: dinner is a meal
sure, as in 'sure, fine', means OK

explanation.surface: A judgment that the standard of a dinner was mostly acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is a standard or yardstick against which things are judged.

clue.text: Vessel containing one last bit of pale amber liquid

indicators.note: the vessel holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: an urn is a vessel
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A container holding the dregs of a pale ale, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests beer; 'amber liquid' is the less pleasant fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Urine is typically a pale yellow to amber bodily fluid, a jokey euphemistic description.

clue.text: Chewy stuff made from corn for grinding on sides of ledge

parts.note: grist is grain brought to the mill to be ground

indicators.note: the two outside letters of the next word are taken

explanation.surface: Something chewy made from grain milled on a shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Gristle is tough cartilage in meat that takes a lot of chewing.

clue.text: Profitable hostilities with Dutch essential to troubled reign

indicators.note: being essential to something places this piece at its heart
troubled signals the letters of reign are disturbed

parts.note: war is open hostilities

explanation.surface: A war with the Dutch proving profitable to a troubled monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' shuffles the five letters of the monarch's rule so that the war and the Dutch can sit, as 'essential to' says, at its heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rewarding pays back well, giving profit or satisfaction.

clue.text: Shrub found in Colorado and California

parts.note: CO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Colorado
CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A plant growing in two neighbouring western US states.
explanation.definitionFit: Coca is a South American bush whose leaves are the source of cocaine.

clue.text: Pen used round old lines in artwork

indicators.note: the pen is placed around the following pieces

parts.note: a cage is a pen for animals
L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: An artist sketching outlines with a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' is the enclosure, not the writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A collage is a picture made by gluing scraps of paper and other materials to a backing.

clue.text: Fabric company clothing most of band with narrow stripe

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap around it, so CO goes round the next piece
most of the word means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a ring is a band, as worn on a finger
a line is a narrow stripe

explanation.surface: A clothing firm dressing a pop group in pinstripes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabric' and 'clothing' both suggest dressmaking; here 'clothing' just means wrapping round, and 'most of' docks the band's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Crinoline was originally a stiff fabric of horsehair and linen, later the hooped petticoat made from it.

clue.text: Composer's toasted sandwiches have a good filling

definitions.note: read as 'composer is', with the 's acting as the link to the wordplay

indicators.note: the following pieces fill the sandwiches

parts.note: panini are Italian toasted sandwiches

explanation.surface: A composer's grilled sandwiches with a tasty filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini was an Italian violin virtuoso who wrote famous caprices and concertos.

clue.text: Barrier to one special female (retired) working for royal mistress

parts.note: a wall is a barrier
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: retired means going back, so these pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: Miss is the title of a girl or unmarried woman
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A retired single woman working as a court official's mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallis Simpson was the American divorcée for whom Edward VIII abdicated in 1936 so as to marry her.

clue.text: Heavy rain initially delayed every London Underground going east

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the next five words

explanation.surface: A downpour delaying every eastbound Tube train.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge is a torrential downpour or flood.

clue.text: Bullfighter charged with endless love

parts.note: to charge is to rush, so tore means charged

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is removed

parts.note: to love is to adore

explanation.surface: A matador who charged in, driven by undying love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' suggests the bull, but it gives TORE; 'endless' trims ADORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A toreador is a bullfighter, especially one on horseback, as in Carmen.

clue.text: Unpleasant character wished to go by horse

parts.note: bade, past of bid, means wished, as in bade farewell
gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: Someone who wanted to travel on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad egg is an idiom for a dishonest or worthless person.

clue.text: Repulsive tip of aromatic herb torn apart

indicators.note: the tip is the first letter of the following word
torn apart signals the letters of herb and torn are broken up

explanation.surface: The leafy end of a fragrant herb being ripped to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrent means loathsome, provoking disgust or hatred.

clue.text: Plant containing source of metallic element

indicators.note: the plant holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: a geranium is a flowering plant

indicators.note: the source is the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A plant that takes up a metal from the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Germanium is a grey metalloid chemical element, number 32, used in semiconductors.

clue.text: Priest stopping religious festival before mice spread an outbreak of the plague?

indicators.note: the priest stops up the festival, sitting inside it

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim religious festival

indicators.note: spread signals the letters of mice scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A priest disrupting a festival before mice spread the plague.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is a widespread occurrence of disease; the question mark admits plague is only one example.

clue.text: Cathedral city where church converted Sartre

indicators.note: converted signals that the letters of Sartre are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: The place where the atheist philosopher Sartre found religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartres, south-west of Paris, is famous for its Gothic cathedral.

clue.text: Nurse carrying cocoa mixed for animal

indicators.note: the nurse carries the next piece inside

parts.note: RN, registered nurse, is an abbreviation for a nurse

indicators.note: mixed signals that the letters of cocoa are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A nurse bringing a mug of cocoa for a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The raccoon is a ring-tailed North American mammal with a masked face.

clue.text: See 9
Suggest leaving end of webbing out of panel strengthening garment

indicators.note: out, as in put out of order, signals that the remaining letters are rearranged
leaving means the next letter departs from the word
the end is the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A tailor's tip about dropping the webbing from a strengthening panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes G (from 'end of') out of SUGGEST, and 'out' rearranges SUGEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A gusset is a triangular piece of fabric sewn in to reinforce or enlarge a garment.

clue.text: Colonist's dog crossing lake

definitions.note: read as 'colonist is', the 's acting as the link to the wordplay

indicators.note: the dog goes across, with the lake inside it

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A pioneer's dog wading across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler is a person who moves to a new land and makes a home there, a colonist.

clue.text: Corporal returned with new mail to give out

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Corp is the abbreviation for corporal

indicators.note: new signals the letters of mail are made into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A soldier returning with fresh post to hand out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' makes PROC; 'new' rearranges MAIL to LAIM.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim is to announce publicly, to give out news.

clue.text: Scientific study of works claiming most of credit

indicators.note: the works take hold of the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: ops, short for opera (opus), are musical works

indicators.note: most of the word means its final letter goes

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A research project on works that take most of the credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims TICK to TIC; buying 'on tick' is British for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Optics is the branch of physics concerned with light and vision.

clue.text: Fruit endlessly given to posh smart brown ape

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an orange is a fruit
U stands for upper-class, hence posh
tan is a smart light brown shade

explanation.surface: Fruit handed to a posh ape in a dapper brown outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang-utan is a red-haired great ape of Borneo and Sumatra.

clue.text: Husband contributing to essential part of housework?

indicators.note: the husband contributes by going into the middle of the next piece

parts.note: the core is the essential part

explanation.surface: A husband doing his bit with the cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A chore is a routine domestic task; housework is an example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Liner after refit carrying old oil

indicators.note: the ship carries the next piece inside it
a refit rebuilds a ship, so the letters of liner are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship, newly refitted, carrying a cargo of old oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after refit' rearranges LINER to NERLI; 'carrying' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Neroli is a fragrant essential oil distilled from bitter orange blossom, used in perfume.

clue.text: Family heir required to eat every bit of spring onion

indicators.note: eating puts the next piece inside the heir

parts.note: a scion is a descendant or heir of a family
all means every bit

explanation.surface: A young heir told to finish every scrap of the vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallion is a spring onion, the usual American name for it.

clue.text: See 22
Group of live animals discovered by yours truly leading horse by lake

parts.note: yours truly is a jocular way to say me
a nag is an old horse
Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A writer discovering animals while leading a horse by a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for exhibition.
